metadata.title: Implement Error Display with User Guidance

story.iWant: clear, helpful error messages when something goes wrong
story.soThat: I understand the issue and know how to proceed
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Create ErrorDisplay component structure (AC: 1) - [ ] Create file: `components/ErrorDisplay.tsx` - [ ] Define ErrorDisplayProps interface with error and onRetry properties - [ ] Import necessary Shadcn UI components (Alert) - [ ] Set up component skeleton with TypeScript strict mode - [ ] Add comprehensive JSDoc documentation
- [ ] Task 2: Implement user-friendly error message mapping (AC: 1) - [ ] Map 'invalid_location' error to "Location not found" message - [ ] Map 'service_unavailable' error to "Unable to get forecast right now. Please try again in a few moments." - [ ] Map 'timeout' error to "Request timed out. Please check your connection and try again." - [ ] Map 'network_error' error to "Network connection failed. Please check your internet and try again." - [ ] Add fallback message for unknown error types - [ ] Ensure no technical details (status codes, stack traces) are shown to users
- [ ] Task 3: Display location suggestions for invalid_location errors (AC: 1) - [ ] Check if error.suggestions array exists and has items - [ ] Render suggestions as a clickable/copyable list - [ ] Display message: "Did you mean one of these?" - [ ] Format suggestions clearly (e.g., "San Francisco, CA") - [ ] Make suggestions visually distinct from error message
- [ ] Task 4: Style error display clearly but not alarming (AC: 1) - [ ] Use Shadcn UI Alert component with variant="destructive" or custom styling - [ ] Apply error color scheme (red tones) that's clear but not harsh - [ ] Use glassmorphic pattern consistent with other components if appropriate - [ ] Add error icon or indicator (⚠️ or Alert icon) - [ ] Ensure readable typography and spacing - [ ] Test responsive design across mobile, tablet, desktop
- [ ] Task 5: Implement screen reader accessibility (AC: 1) - [ ] Add aria-live="assertive" for immediate error announcement - [ ] Use semantic HTML (Alert role or appropriate ARIA role) - [ ] Ensure error message text is clear and descriptive - [ ] Test that suggestions are accessible if present - [ ] Verify role="alert" or equivalent is applied
- [ ] Task 6: Ensure input field remains accessible after error (AC: 1) - [ ] Verify error display doesn't disable or hide location input - [ ] Confirm input field is still enabled and focusable - [ ] Test that user can immediately retry with new location - [ ] Ensure error clears when new search is submitted - [ ] Verify focus management returns to input after error display
- [ ] Task 7: Integrate ErrorDisplay into main page component (AC: 1) - [ ] Import ErrorDisplay in `app/page.tsx` - [ ] Add error state management (useState for error data) - [ ] Conditionally render ErrorDisplay when error state is present - [ ] Pass error response and retry handler to ErrorDisplay - [ ] Clear error state when new search begins - [ ] Test error state transitions (error → retry → loading → answer/error)
- [ ] Task 8: Test all error scenarios (AC: 1) - [ ] Test invalid_location error display (with and without suggestions) - [ ] Test service_unavailable error display - [ ] Test timeout error display - [ ] Test network_error error display - [ ] Verify each error shows appropriate message - [ ] Confirm input remains accessible in all error states - [ ] Test retry functionality clears error and initiates new search
- [ ] Task 9: Validate accessibility compliance (AC: 1) - [ ] Run Lighthouse accessibility audit - [ ] Test keyboard navigation (Tab to error, Tab to input) - [ ] Verify screen reader announcements (use VoiceOver/NVDA if available) - [ ] Check aria-live region is working - [ ] Ensure error color contrast meets WCAG standards - [ ] Verify focus indicators are visible
- [ ] Task 10: Validate code quality and testing standards (AC: 1) - [ ] Run TypeScript type checking: `npm run type-check` (0 errors) - [ ] Run ESLint validation: `npm run lint` (0 warnings) - [ ] Verify responsive design at 320px, 768px, 1024px breakpoints - [ ] Test all error types in browser - [ ] Confirm error → retry flow works seamlessly - [ ] Document testing results in completion notes

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** an error occurs during the request **When** the error is displayed **Then** a user-friendly error message is shown (not technical details) **And** invalid location errors show helpful suggestions if available **And** API failure shows: "Error - Please check back later" **And** network errors show clear connectivity messaging **And** the input field remains accessible to retry **And** error messages are announced to screen readers **And** error styling is clear but not alarming

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.section: AC-7: Error States Display User-Friendly Messages
doc.snippet: Error Response Contract: ErrorResponse interface with error codes (invalid_location, service_unavailable, timeout, network_error), user-friendly messages, and optional suggestions array for location errors. Frontend must map error codes to clear, non-technical messages.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: ErrorDisplay component is presentational with error state and retry callback. Props: { error: ErrorResponse, onRetry: () => void }. Single component handles all error types using conditional rendering. Styling uses Shadcn UI Alert or custom glassmorphic card.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.section: Data Models and Contracts - ErrorResponse Interface
doc.snippet: interface ErrorResponse { error: 'invalid_location' | 'service_unavailable' | 'timeout' | 'network_error'; message: string; suggestions?: string[]; }. Backend returns structured error responses with error codes. Frontend can use backend message or override with custom message.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Error Recovery Flow: User submits → API fails → ErrorDisplay renders → Input remains enabled → User corrects/waits → New search → Error clears → Loading begins → New answer/error displays. Always maintain input accessibility.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Error messages must use aria-live="assertive" for immediate announcement, role="alert" for semantic meaning, semantic HTML structure, keyboard navigation support, and clear screen reader text. Loading uses polite, errors use assertive.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: Frontend API Client Pattern: Catch fetch errors and map to ErrorResponse. Network errors return { error: 'network_error', message: '...' }. HTTP status codes: 400 (invalid request), 404 (location not found), 500 (server error), 504 (timeout).

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: Error Codes: invalid_location (location not found), service_unavailable (API failure/5xx), timeout (request >5s), network_error (connectivity issue). All errors must fail gracefully with user-friendly messages.

doc.title: Story 3.6: Implement Close Call Messaging
doc.snippet: CloseCallBadge uses: backdrop-blur-md bg-white/10 border-white/20 with amber color scheme (neutral, not alarming). ErrorDisplay should use similar pattern but with error colors: bg-red-50/90 border-red-200 while maintaining glassmorphic effect and visual consistency.

doc.title: Story 3.6: Implement Close Call Messaging
doc.snippet: CloseCallBadge uses semantic HTML without explicit ARIA role (informational). ErrorDisplay requires role="alert" and aria-live="assertive" for critical error announcements. Screen readers need immediate notification of errors (assertive vs polite).

story-context.constraints:
**Component Structure:** - ErrorDisplay must be a client component ("use client" directive not required if only presentational, parent handles state) - Single component handles all error types using conditional rendering (no separate components per error type) - Props interface: ErrorDisplayProps { error: ErrorResponse; onRetry?: () => void; } - Component must return null or empty fragment when error is null (defensive programming)
**Error Message Mapping (User-Friendly):** - invalid_location: "Location not found." (append "Did you mean one of these?" if suggestions exist) - service_unavailable: "Unable to get forecast right now. Please try again in a few moments." - timeout: "Request timed out. Please check your connection and try again." - network_error: "Network connection failed. Please check your internet and try again." - Fallback for unknown errors: "Something went wrong. Please try again." - NEVER show technical details (status codes, stack traces, error.name) to users
**Styling Constraints:** - Use glassmorphic pattern: backdrop-blur-md with semi-transparent backgrounds - Error color scheme: bg-red-50/90 border-red-200 or similar soft red tones (not harsh red) - Alternatively: Use Shadcn UI Alert component with variant="destructive" - Error icon: ⚠️ emoji or Shadcn UI alert icon (lucide-react AlertCircle) - Maintain visual consistency with CloseCallBadge and DetailCard components - Responsive design: Works at 320px, 768px, 1024px+ breakpoints
**Accessibility Constraints:** - Must include aria-live="assertive" for immediate screen reader announcement - Must include role="alert" for semantic error indication - Use semantic HTML (not just styled divs) - Error message text must be descriptive and screen-reader friendly - Suggestions list (if present) must be accessible with proper list structure - Focus management: Input field must remain focusable after error displays
**Integration Constraints:** - ErrorDisplay integrates into page.tsx at line 174 (after AnswerDisplay) - Conditional rendering: {errorData && } - Error state clears when new search begins (setErrorData(null) in handleSubmit) - onRetry handler is optional - can simply refocus input or clear error state - Must not disable or hide input field when error displays
**Testing Requirements (Epic 3 Manual Testing Strategy):** - NO automated unit tests required (deferred to Epic 5.7) - Manual browser testing on http://localhost:3000 - Test all error types: invalid_location (with/without suggestions), service_unavailable, timeout, network_error - TypeScript validation: npm run type-check (0 errors) - ESLint validation: npm run lint (0 warnings) - Lighthouse accessibility audit (score > 95) - Responsive design testing at 320px, 768px, 1024px breakpoints

tests.standards:
**Epic 3 Testing Strategy:** Manual browser testing is the primary approach for Epic 3. Automated unit tests are deferred to Epic 5.7. Testing standards:
1. **TypeScript Type Checking:** All code must pass `npm run type-check` with 0 errors. No 'any' types allowed.
2. **ESLint Validation:** All code must pass `npm run lint` with 0 warnings. Follow Next.js and React best practices.
3. **Manual Functional Testing:** Test all error scenarios in browser at http://localhost:3000. Verify error messages, suggestions, input accessibility, retry flow.
4. **Accessibility Testing:** - Lighthouse accessibility audit (score > 95) - Keyboard navigation testing (Tab order, focus management) - Screen reader testing with VoiceOver (macOS) or NVDA (Windows) if available - ARIA compliance: role="alert", aria-live="assertive"
5. **Responsive Design Testing:** Use browser DevTools responsive mode to test at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Verify no horizontal scrolling, readable text, proper layout.
6. **Cross-Browser Testing:** Primary development in Chrome. Basic compatibility check in Safari and Firefox (comprehensive cross-browser testing deferred to Epic 4.7).

tests.ideas:
**Test Case 1: Invalid Location Error with Suggestions** - Mock/trigger invalid_location error with suggestions array - Verify: "Location not found." message displays - Verify: "Did you mean one of these?" section displays - Verify: Suggestions list renders clearly (e.g., "San Francisco, CA", "San Francisco, TX") - Verify: Input field remains enabled and accessible - Verify: Error clears when new search is submitted
**Test Case 2: Invalid Location Error without Suggestions** - Mock/trigger invalid_location error without suggestions array - Verify: "Location not found." message displays - Verify: No suggestions section appears - Verify: No crash or undefined errors - Verify: Input remains accessible for retry
**Test Case 3: Service Unavailable Error** - Mock/trigger service_unavailable error (backend 500 error) - Verify: Message "Unable to get forecast right now. Please try again in a few moments." displays - Verify: No suggestions or additional content - Verify: Input remains enabled - Verify: Retry flow works correctly
**Test Case 4: Timeout Error** - Mock/trigger timeout error (request >5s) - Verify: Message "Request timed out. Please check your connection and try again." displays - Verify: Input remains accessible
**Test Case 5: Network Error** - Simulate network offline or connectivity failure - Verify: Message "Network connection failed. Please check your internet and try again." displays - Verify: Input remains accessible
**Test Case 6: Unknown/Fallback Error** - Mock/trigger error with unexpected error code - Verify: Fallback message "Something went wrong. Please try again." displays - Verify: Graceful degradation (no crash)
**Test Case 7: Error → Retry → Success Flow** - Display error → Enter new valid location → Submit - Verify: Error clears when loading state begins - Verify: Loading state displays - Verify: New answer displays correctly (no error state pollution)
**Test Case 8: Error → Retry → New Error Flow** - Display error → Enter new invalid location → Submit - Verify: Old error clears - Verify: New error displays correctly - Verify: No state pollution between errors
**Test Case 9: Accessibility - Keyboard Navigation** - Display error → Tab through interface - Verify: Error message is accessible via keyboard - Verify: Input field is still focusable - Verify: Submit button is still accessible - Verify: Tab order is logical
**Test Case 10: Accessibility - Screen Reader** - Display error with VoiceOver/NVDA active - Verify: Error is announced immediately (aria-live="assertive") - Verify: Error message text is read clearly - Verify: Suggestions (if present) are accessible and read correctly
**Test Case 11: Responsive Design** - Test error display at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop) - Verify: Error message is readable without zooming - Verify: Suggestions list wraps properly on narrow screens - Verify: No horizontal scrolling - Verify: Layout is professional and clear at all breakpoints
**Test Case 12: Visual Styling** - Verify: Error uses soft red color scheme (not harsh/alarming) - Verify: Glassmorphic effect or Alert component styling is consistent - Verify: Error icon displays clearly - Verify: Text is readable with sufficient contrast - Verify: Spacing and padding are comfortable
